plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant shrubs march across the Provençal plateaus in ribbons of violet-blue, humming with bees and perfuming the warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August, with true lavender at its best from late June to mid-July
plants.funFact: Lavender's name is thought to come from the Latin 'lavare', to wash, as the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dinner-plate-sized flower head of pointed pink bracts surrounds a silky, crown-like center, blazing against the cool, misty winter landscape of the Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: April to October, which includes the Southern Hemisphere winter
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its lineage is ancient enough to have flourished before the continents fully separated.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Rising on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves, goblet-shaped blossoms unfurl at dawn in pink and white across still summer ponds.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to July in temperate Asia, often into August
plants.location: Temperate Asia, including ponds in Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves shed water and dirt thanks to a microscopic surface texture, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect'.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy petals surround spiky copper-orange cones, drawing butterflies and goldfinches to prairies and sunny gardens.
plants.location: Central and eastern United States prairies and gardens
plants.funFact: The spiky central cone gives the genus its name, from the Greek 'echinos' for hedgehog.
